```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

This file walks once through the project checklist on a small example. It is a
template for the structure of your analysis, not a model answer for your data.
Data: `MASS::birthwt` (189 births at Baystate Medical Center, Springfield, Massachusetts, 1986).

## 1. Question

Is maternal smoking associated with low birth weight (< 2.5 kg), after adjusting for the
mother's weight, age, race and history of hypertension? Goal: **explanation** (an adjusted
odds ratio with its uncertainty), not prediction.

## 2. Data and EDA

```{r data}
library(tidyverse)
library(mgcv)
bw <- MASS::birthwt |>
  mutate(low = as.integer(low),
         smoke = factor(smoke, levels = 0:1, labels = c("no", "yes")),
         race = factor(race, levels = 1:3, labels = c("white", "black", "other")),
         ht = factor(ht, levels = 0:1, labels = c("no", "yes")))
nrow(bw); sum(bw$low)                 # 189 births, 59 low birth weight
bw |> group_by(smoke) |> summarise(n = n(), p_low = mean(low))
summary(bw$lwt)                       # mother's weight in pounds
```

Structure: one row per birth, independent mothers, binary response. That points to a
binomial GLM; a smooth term (GAM) checks whether the effect of weight or age is linear on
the logit scale. With 59 events, keep the model small (about 10 events per parameter).

## 3. Two model classes

```{r models}
m_glm <- glm(low ~ smoke + lwt + age + race + ht, family = binomial, data = bw)
m_gam <- gam(low ~ smoke + s(lwt) + s(age) + race + ht, family = binomial, data = bw,
             method = "REML")
summary(m_gam)$s.table               # edf close to 1 means "linear is enough"
AIC(m_glm, m_gam)
```

Both models are fitted to the same binary response with the same likelihood, so AIC is a
valid comparison. A smooth with edf near 1 adds nothing over a linear term.

## 4. Diagnostics

Raw residuals for a binary response fall on two curves and say little. Binned residuals
average the residuals within groups of similar fitted values; about 95% of the bins should
lie inside $\pm 2\,\mathrm{se}$.

```{r binned, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
binned_resid <- function(fit, nbins = 10) {
  tibble(p = fitted(fit), r = bw$low - fitted(fit)) |>
    mutate(bin = cut_number(p, nbins)) |>
    group_by(bin) |>
    summarise(p_mean = mean(p), r_mean = mean(r),
              se = sqrt(mean(p) * (1 - mean(p)) / n()), .groups = "drop")
}
br <- binned_resid(m_glm)
ggplot(br, aes(p_mean, r_mean)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = -2 * se, ymax = 2 * se), fill = "grey85") +
  geom_point(size = 2.5) + geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = 2) +
  labs(x = "Mean fitted probability in bin", y = "Mean residual in bin")
mean(abs(br$r_mean) <= 2 * br$se)    # share of bins inside the band
```

Influence: the largest Cook's distances.

```{r influence}
sort(cooks.distance(m_glm), decreasing = TRUE)[1:3]
```

## 5. Interpretation with uncertainty

```{r or}
est <- coef(summary(m_glm))["smokeyes", ]
or  <- exp(est["Estimate"] + c(0, -1.96, 1.96) * est["Std. Error"])
round(setNames(or, c("OR", "lower", "upper")), 2)
exp(confint(m_glm)["smokeyes", ])    # profile-likelihood interval
```

**Sentence for the report.** Among mothers of the same weight, age, race and hypertension
status, the odds of a low-birth-weight baby are estimated to be 2.9 times higher for smokers
(95% CI 1.4 to 6.2; profile-likelihood interval 1.4 to 6.4). This is an observational association: smokers may differ from
non-smokers in ways the model does not capture.

## 6. Communication: one figure

```{r figure, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
nd <- expand_grid(lwt = seq(90, 250, by = 5), smoke = c("no", "yes"),
                  age = 23, race = "white", ht = "no")
pr <- predict(m_glm, newdata = nd, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
nd <- nd |> mutate(fit = plogis(pr$fit), lo = plogis(pr$fit - 1.96 * pr$se.fit),
                   hi = plogis(pr$fit + 1.96 * pr$se.fit))
ggplot(nd, aes(lwt, fit, colour = smoke, fill = smoke)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lo, ymax = hi), alpha = 0.2, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Mother's weight (lb)", y = "P(low birth weight)", colour = "Smoker", fill = "Smoker",
       caption = "White mothers aged 23 without hypertension; 95% pointwise intervals")
```

Intervals are computed on the logit scale and transformed, so they stay inside $(0, 1)$.
